Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

1. Create a workspace named "temp_workspace" and obtain a copy of the system group database saved as "temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt" (retrieve the live /etc/group data into that file).  
2. Clean and parse "temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt" by removing comment lines and blank lines, extract the group name field from each remaining entry into "temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt", and record the original and cleaned line counts in "temp_workspace/cleanup_log.txt".  
3. Produce a deduplicated list from "temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt" saved as "temp_workspace/groups_unique.txt", record a checksum and timestamp for that file in "temp_workspace/groups_verification.txt", and note that the unique-list file is ready for determining the total number of groups.

{"script":"mkdir -p temp_workspace
cp /etc/group temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt
orig=$(wc -l < temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt)
awk '/^[[:space:]]*#/ {next} /^[[:space:]]*$/ {next} {print}' temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt | cut -d: -f1 > temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt
clean=$(wc -l < temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt)
printf "original_lines:%s\ncleaned_lines:%s\n" "$orig" "$clean" > temp_workspace/cleanup_log.txt
sort -u temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt > temp_workspace/groups_unique.txt
sha256sum temp_workspace/groups_unique.txt > temp_workspace/groups_verification.txt
date --iso-8601=seconds >> temp_workspace/groups_verification.txt
echo "unique-list ready for determining the total number of groups" >> temp_workspace/groups_verification.txt
wc -l < temp_workspace/groups_unique.txt
"}
